subject: Banking
title: The Roadshow Spectacle
description: A quick, practical guide to The Roadshow Spectacle.

hook.text: Before an IPO, executives travel to 20+ cities in two weeks pitching their company to investors. This is the roadshow.

buildup.text: Roadshows include breakfast meetings in London, lunch in Frankfurt, dinner in New York. Every meal is a sales pitch.

discovery.text: Institutional investors use roadshows to decide how many shares to request. Their demand determines the final IPO price.

twist.text: Virtual roadshows emerged during COVID. Some companies now skip physical tours entirely.

climax.text: Roadshows are theater. The goal is creating FOMO among investors so demand exceeds supply and the price rises.

punchline.text: 20 cities in two weeks. The IPO roadshow is a sales marathon.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of an IPO roadshow?
options: Generate investor demand and determine final share pricing

details.summary: An IPO roadshow is a multi-city presentation tour where company executives and investment bankers pitch the company's story to institutional investors over one to two weeks, gauging demand and building the order book that determines the offering price.
details.whyItMatters: The roadshow is where the IPO price is really set. Institutional investor enthusiasm or skepticism during these meetings directly determines how much money the company raises and at what valuation it enters public markets.
takeaways: Executives present to hundreds of institutional investors over two weeks
Banks build an order book based on investor interest and price sensitivity
Strong roadshow demand leads to higher pricing and oversubscription

faq.question: What happens during a typical roadshow meeting?
faq.answer: The CEO and CFO present the company's financials, growth strategy, and competitive position. Institutional investors ask tough questions about risks and projections. Bankers track each investor's interest level and potential allocation size.

faq.question: Can a bad roadshow kill an IPO?
faq.answer: Yes. If institutional investors show weak demand, the company may need to lower the price range or postpone the offering entirely. WeWork's failed 2019 IPO attempt died partly because investor scrutiny during the preparation phase killed demand.
